Triage: re-laned `domain:examples` → **`domain:identity`**, held as `finding`. `domain:examples` is not a lane-table label; per the table, `examples/*` cards belong to the subsystem they exercise, and this one exercises position ↔ permission-set binding (`plugin-security` semantics demonstrated by `examples/app-crm/src/security/*`). Type intent if promoted: **Task**.

Grading input for the findings round: the filer's own grade is right — nothing hits this today (no seeded persona users; binding is an admin action in real deployments). The pull toward fixing is teaching-surface consistency: the CRM example currently demonstrates the two declarations *never meeting*, the exact shape #8059 shows apps copy from examples. Cheapest alignment is the showcase's own pattern (a `bind-position-sets`-style hook) rather than `isDefault`, which would change who gets the grants. Not urgent; do not promote ahead of the queue's live defects.

Triage (findings round): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, stays `domain:identity` (examples route to the subsystem they exercise; this one exercises positions/permission-sets), type Bug.

Grading rationale: the "product call" the card defers is already answered by in-repo precedent — the showcase binds positions to sets imperatively in `src/security/bind-position-sets.ts` on `kernel:bootstrapped`, so the platform's demonstrated pattern is *bind, don't leave the halves floating*. An example that declares 3 positions and grants none of them anything is a Bug by the declared≠functional test, and examples are exactly what AI authors copy — a broken pattern here reproduces downstream (the AI-error-resistance lens is what promotes this over a shrug). Direction ruled: mirror the showcase's `bind-position-sets` hook (⛔ not `isDefault` — that would grant every user, which changes the example's security story rather than completing it). The 18/18 probe-blocked readout from #7978's personas is the acceptance test: after the fix, the three personas should prove their granted objects.

Size/model suggestion: S/M, `sonnet` (mechanical mirror of an existing in-repo pattern with a measurable pass criterion).

⚠️ **`sonnet` is a deliberate choice, not a default, and this is the first card this shift to get it.** The tiering policy puts the floor at `sonnet` for mechanical cards — where correctness is decided by a machine-checkable criterion and the failure mode is a missed gate rather than a judgement error. This card qualifies on both counts: the **direction is already ruled** by triage (mirror the showcase hook; ⛔ not `isDefault`), and the acceptance criterion is a **measured readout**, not an opinion — #7978's per-position probe personas currently report `18 of 18 probe-blocked` and must report the granted objects as proven afterwards. Sending `opus` at a ruled, machine-verified mirror of an existing in-repo pattern would be the same misallocation as sending `sonnet` at a design call, just in the cheaper direction.

## The ruling this executes (triage findings round, 17:53Z)

> Direction ruled: mirror the showcase's `bind-position-sets` hook (⛔ **not** `isDefault` — that would grant every user, which changes the example's security story rather than completing it). The 18/18 probe-blocked readout from #7978's personas is the acceptance test.

The card itself deferred this as "a product call for triage"; triage answered it from in-repo precedent rather than inventing one — the showcase already binds imperatively on `kernel:bootstrapped`, so the platform's demonstrated pattern is *bind, don't leave the halves floating*.

⚠️ **Why this is a Bug rather than a shrug, in triage's words and worth carrying into the dispatch**: an example that declares three positions and grants none of them anything is broken by the declared≠functional test, **and examples are what AI authors copy** — a broken pattern here reproduces downstream. That is the AI-error-resistance lens deciding a card that measured business pull alone would have left sitting.

**PM review: ACCEPT** — PR #8167. Seat #6022, session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`. CI convergence is mine.

## Verified against GitHub

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| Path face | ✅ 3 files, zero fork triggers |
| ⛔ `packages/**` out of surface | ✅ **untouched** — example-only, as ruled |
| ⛔ `isDefault` not used | ✅ — both hits in the diff are **prose explaining why it was rejected** (changeset + a code comment: *"deliberately NOT marked `isDefault`: that would auto-bind it to the `everyone` anchor and grant every user"*) |
| Mirrors the showcase hook | ✅ new `bind-position-sets.ts` + an `onEnable` export |

## ⚠️ The ruled acceptance criterion was not met as literally worded — and that is correct

Triage wrote: *"after the fix, the three personas should **prove** their granted objects."* Your readout is `proven = 0`.

I checked your explanation rather than accepting it, because "the criterion doesn't apply to me" is exactly the claim that needs verifying. It holds:

- the five objects `crm_sales_user` grants — `account`, `activity`, `contact`, `lead`, `opportunity` — **all declare `sharingModel: 'public_read_write'`**;
- so the verify tool classifies them **member-visible (inconclusive)**, not `proven`, by design — an org-wide read+write object cannot produce an rls-consistent verdict.

**The literal criterion was unreachable by construction, no matter what the fix did.** You noticed that and said so, instead of claiming success against it or contorting the binding to chase it. That is the right handling of a criterion that turns out to be wrong.

The signal that actually moves: **`probeBlocked` 18 → 3**, zero RLS holes in both states, and the three residual blocks are all `crm_opportunity_line_item` — an object `crm_sales_user` never granted at all, which is a **different defect** (filed as #8164, and independently flagged by the platform's own `security-master-detail-ungranted` build lint). So `Fixes #8060` is right: the card is "three declared positions bound to nothing", and they are now bound.

## The reverse verification is what makes this a `sonnet` card that lands rather than one that merely compiles

> disabled the `onEnable` wiring, re-ran, got back the **exact** pre-fix 18/18 probeBlocked baseline; re-enabled and re-confirmed

A binding registered on a hook that never fires would leave the readout unchanged and look like a no-op fix — I named that hazard in the dispatch and you closed it by measurement in both directions. Returning to the *exact* baseline (not merely "worse") is what rules out a partially-firing hook.

## On the model tier, since this was the first `sonnet` card of the shift

It was the right call, and now for a checkable reason rather than a hopeful one: every judgement this card needed had already been made — direction ruled by triage, pattern existing in-repo, acceptance measured by a tool. What was left was execution plus honest reporting, and both are here. ⚠️ The one genuinely non-mechanical moment — noticing the acceptance criterion was unreachable — was handled by *reporting* it rather than deciding around it, which is what the tier expects.

## Next (mine)

Per-job gate conclusions, then flip ready → arm. I will read `check:objectui-pin-fresh` specifically: you report it red and **pre-existing ambient staleness** with reasoning (it depends only on `.objectui-sha` vs objectui's remote main, not on this diff). ⛔ I will confirm that independently before arming rather than take it on the note — a "pre-existing red" is the single easiest thing to be wrong about.
